CLOUD FIXER seat for tvofi/heatpump_optimizer, topic r10-mutation-anchor, at head 50af6174f53c0f9bec3f705c3a4bb99615f71acc. Never send push notifications. Write no Claude Code footer, no Co-Authored-By or Claude-Session trailer and no claude.ai session link in any commit, pull-request body or comment you produce; check your commits with `git log --format=%B` before pushing.
Setup: `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin`. The toolchain (venv python, node, gh) is on PATH from the environment. Run anything heavy in the background with Monitor and no timeout.
Role: read dev/governance/roles/fixer.md and CLAUDE.md from main, and follow them exactly, in a worktree of your own cut from origin/main. Fetch 50af6174f53c0f9bec3f705c3a4bb99615f71acc for the base you were given.
Output: push the code to refs/heads/handoff/r10-mutation-anchor, then write the PR body and run `bash tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh r10-mutation-anchor <body.md>`, which pushes refs/heads/handoff-body/r10-mutation-anchor; that second push is the return signal. Push nothing else, open no pull request and write no delivery row. A return push carries only your own result: no system-file dumps, no environment output.
Never write to any branch except your return refs. Never work around a hook or a refusal; report it in your result instead.

Brief (snapshotted when this payload was rendered):
Fix the vacuous kill in the entities.py `--anchor` mutation self-test soundly, and measure how many of the 123 `killed_by: tests/entities.py` pins are vacuous. Seams: tests/mutation_table.py (the mutation instrument) and the R9-F10.13 block of tests/entities.py; the pins live under tests/mutation_ledger/killed_by. Deliverables: (1) a failing test first: an equivalent rewrite of a pinned line (the control above) must NOT be reported killed under `--pin-killed`; (2) the fix, so that a kill is attributed only to a check that fails on the mutant and passes on the base, not to the ledger/inventory disagreement the pin itself causes (for example, drive the anchor against a tree whose ledger is the base's, or exclude the pinned line's own pin from the comparison); (3) the measurement: for each of the 123 pins, whether its line carries a second pin and whether the kill survives the fix, with the count of vacuous pins printed beside the count of pins checked, compared as sets and not totals; (4) the vacuous pins re-proven with a real kill or struck with the reason. A fix that lowers the count of proven pins is a measurement change: the ledger is data, not a ratchet, but state the before and after counts in the pull request.

FINDING (forward-carried from R10-SAV-BASELINE, #2255, PR #2411; no group owned tests/mutation_table.py or the R9-F10.13 block of tests/entities.py until this one). `tests/entities.py`'s `--anchor` self-test runs `mutation_table.main` against the live tree, and `clone_tree` overlays the working tree. So under `--pin-killed`, entities.py "kills" every mutant of a line that already carries a pin, by refusing the ledger/inventory disagreement, not by a check that sees the mutation. Control: the equivalent rewrite `if 0 < dt:` of the `dt` guard in `MonthlyLedger` (a line of PR #2411's head, in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/ledger.py; not yet on main) fails the same single check, so the kill is vacuous (an equivalent mutant is "killed"). Re-measure: at a later head, mutate any pinned line equivalently, and run `env -u BASH_ENV PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py`; the equivalent rewrite must survive. Until it is fixed, a `killed_by: tests/entities.py` pin on a line with a second pin is unproven. The ledger holds 123 `killed_by: tests/entities.py` pins in all, counted by `grep -rl '"killed_by": "tests/entities.py"' tests/mutation_ledger/killed_by | wc -l`. How many of them sit on a line with a second pin, or are vacuous, is not measured.

Forward-carried (finding-propagation.md): the finding above, with its control and its re-measure, is the acceptance; re-derive the 123 and the second-pin count at your merge base. Part of #201.

Identity and flow: the seat pushes refs only, through tools/audit/seat/handoff_push.sh and tools/audit/seat/bus.sh; every GitHub write is the orchestrator's (decisions 0011 and 0013). Work from fresh origin/main in your own worktree under your ABSOLUTE scratch directory; stop only PIDs you started. Follow dev/governance/roles/fixer.md: failing test first, mutation proof, the finder's harness at both ends, a null control for every quantified claim, `GATE_SCOPE` auto, tests/structure.py before push. Every figure above is a snapshot at the finding's baseline: re-derive it at your merge base. Owner gate: none (the approver App approves). Models: fixer opus, reviewer opus. Closing: the pull request names every issue in this group's `issues` in prose; the orchestrator verifies each intended issue closed after the merge.
